scope_name: FD-P2-lite / non-Shiny-Real complete-metric final results analysis

main_summary.csv_convention: 14 paired-scene rows; each row expands train/test base, rc, delta, and win flag columns for all major metrics.
main_summary.cautious_conclusion: RC strongly improves reflection consistency in the scoped datasets. Render-quality metrics are mixed, so RC should be described as prioritizing consistency with image-quality tradeoffs rather than as globally superior.

wo_ref.scope_limited_interpretation: Removing reflection-consistency supervision degrades aggregate reflection consistency relative to RC on both datasets and both splits. Among the targeted removal variants, this supports reflection-consistency supervision as the stronger contributor to the scoped consistency improvement.
wo_ref.render_quality_interpretation: Render-quality effects are mixed: some PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS aggregates preserve or improve relative to RC while consistency worsens.

wo_conf.scope_limited_interpretation: Neutralizing confidence weighting also degrades aggregate reflection consistency relative to RC on both datasets and both splits, but generally less than wo_ref. Confidence weighting contributes to consistency without yielding a uniform render-quality direction.
wo_conf.render_quality_interpretation: Render-quality effects remain metric- and dataset-dependent; no uniform quality advantage is supported.

rough_only.scope_limited_interpretation: Roughness-only regularization does not reproduce RC reflection-consistency behavior. This control is not a single-component removal, so it supports insufficiency of roughness-only regularization rather than an isolated causal ranking.
rough_only.render_quality_interpretation: Roughness-only render-quality behavior is mixed and often degrades relative to RC, especially on Glossy Synthetic.

ablation_component_interpretation.component_priority_caveat: The scoped paired evidence suggests reflection-consistency supervision is more important than confidence weighting for consistency, while no single component has a uniform render-quality effect. These are scope-limited diagnostic interpretations, not causal claims.

evidence_supported_conclusions: Within the FD-P2-lite / non-Shiny-Real scope, complete-metric coverage is 70/70.
The main base/RC comparison is complete at 28/28 under the full metric set.
The non-Shiny-Real ablation comparison is complete at 42/42 under the full metric set.
RC provides strong evidence for improved reflection consistency in the scoped datasets.
Render-quality metrics show tradeoffs and should be reported separately from reflection-consistency improvements.
Shiny Blender Real remains excluded due to OOM and is not used for full FD-P2 claims.
Original full FD-P2 and full 51-cell ablation claims remain NO-GO.
